chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'If you pray the eclipse prayer until the eclipse passes from the sun and the moon, and you prolong your prayer, then that is superior. And if you wish to pray and finish your prayer before the eclipse passes, that is permissible. And if you do not know until the eclipse passes, then you learn afterwards, there is no eclipse prayer upon you. And if someone informs you while you are sleeping, and you learn, then sleep overcomes you and you do not pray, then you must make it up.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for performing and making up the Islamic eclipse prayer (Salat al-Kusuf)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the flexibility in the duration of the Eclipse Prayer (Salat al-Kusuf), prioritizing a prolonged, contemplative worship that mirrors the celestial event's duration. It provides practical jurisprudential distinctions for missed prayers based on the cause of omission, reflecting the Shia emphasis on intentionality and ease in ritual obligations. The ruling underscores the spiritual significance of the eclipse as a sign of God’s power, encouraging believers to engage deeply with the prayer rather than treating it as a mere formality.
